5631.text:
Match the following species with the correct number of electrons present in them:

Species Number of Electrons
$( i ) {Be}^{2 +}$ $( a ) 0$
$( ii ) H^{+}$ $( b ) 10$
$( iii ) {Na}^{+}$ $( c ) 2$
$( iv ) {Mg}^{+}$ $( d ) 11$
$( e ) 4$

&
options: $( i - a ) , ( ii - b ) , ( iii - c ) , ( iv - d )$
$( i - c ) , ( ii - a ) , ( iii - b ) , ( iv - d )$
5631.sol:
We know that the number of electrons is equal to the atomic number of element in neutral state.

Atomic number of beryllium is $4$ but ${Be}^{2 +}$ can be formed by losing the two electrons& so remaining electrons in ${Be}^{2 +}$ will be $4 - 2 = 2$.

Similarly, the number of electrons in $H^{+}$ is $1 - 1 = 0$.

Similarly, the number of electrons in ${Na}^{+}$ is $11 - 1 = 10$.

Similarly, the number of electrons in ${Mg}^{+}$ is $12 - 1 = 11$.

Hence, the correct match will be $( i - c ) , ( ii - a ) , ( iii - b ) , ( iv - d )$.

options: Both Statement-I and statement-II are correct

5778.sol:
(I) Easily liquefiable gases are adsorbed more easily because higher the critical temperature, higher is the intermolecular force of attraction and easier is the liquefaction.
(II) Physical adsorption is an exothermic process but its enthalpy of adsorption is low $\left(20-40 \mathrm{KJ} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}\right)$
This is because the attraction between gas molecules and solid surface is only due to weak van der Waals forces.
On the other hand, enthalpy of chemisorption is high $-240 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ ) as it involves chemical bond formation.

6286.subject: Mathematics
6286.text: The curve $f ( x ) = {e}^{x}sinx$ is defined in the interval $[ 0, 2\pi ] .$ The value of $x$ for which the slope of the tangent drawn to the curve at $x$ is maximum, is
6286.sol:
Given:

$f ( x ) = {e}^{x}sinx$

We know that the slope of tangent is given by $\left\{\dfrac{dy}{dx} = {f}^{'}\left(x\right)\right\}$.

Now,

${f}^{'} ( x ) = Z = {e}^{x}sinx + {e}^{x}cosx$

$Z = {e}^{x}\left(sinx + cosx\right)$

$\dfrac{dZ}{dx} = {e}^{x}\left(sinx + cosx\right) + {e}^{x}\left(cosx - sinx\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{dZ}{dx} = 2{e}^{x}cosx$

For maxima, $\dfrac{dZ}{dx} = 0$

$⇒ 2{e}^{x}cosx = 0$

$⇒ {e}^{x}cosx = 0$

$∵ {e}^{x} \ne 0, x \in R$ 

$∴ cosx = 0 ⇒ x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{3\pi}{2}; \left\{∵ x \in \left[0, 2\pi\right]\right\}$

Now, 

$⇒ \dfrac{{d}^{2}Z}{d{x}^{2}} = 2{e}^{x}cosx - 2{e}^{x}sinx$

                 $= 2{e}^{x}\left(cosx - sinx\right)$

$\left\{{\left(\dfrac{{d}^{2}Z}{d{x}^{2}}\right)}_{x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}}\right\} = - 2e\dfrac{\pi}{2} < 0 \to \text{MAXIMA}$

And, $\left\{{\left(\dfrac{{d}^{2}Z}{d{x}^{2}}\right)}_{x = \dfrac{3\pi}{2}}\right\} = 2e\dfrac{3\pi}{2} > 0 \to \text{MINIMA}$

Hence, $Z = \dfrac{dy}{dx}\left(\text{slope of tangent}\right)$ is maximum when $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

7937.text: If the determinant $\left|$\begin{array}{ccc}$\cos 2$ x & $\sin ^2 x$ & $\cos 2$ x \\ $\sin ^2 x$ & $\cos 2$ x & $\cos ^2 x$ \\ $\cos 2$ x & $\cos ^2 x$ & $\cos 2$ x\end{array}$\right|$ is expanded in powers of $\cos x$, then the constant term in the expansion is
7937.sol:
Let $\Delta=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\cos 2 x & \sin ^2 x & \cos 2 x \\ \sin ^2 x & \cos 2 x & \cos ^2 x \\ \cos 2 x & \cos ^2 x & \cos 2 x\end{array}\right|$
On expanding along $R_1$. $\begin{aligned}& \Delta=\cos2 x\left[\cos ^2 2 x-\cos ^4 x\right]-\sin ^2 x \\
& {\left[\sin ^2 x \cos 2 x-\cos ^2 x \cdot \cos2 x\right]} \\
& +\cos 2 x\left[\sin ^2 x \cos ^2 x-\cos ^2 2 x\right] \\
& \Delta=\cos2 x\left[\left(2 \cos ^2 x-1\right)^2-\cos ^4 x\right] \\
& -\sin ^2 x\left[\cos2 x\left(\sin ^2 x-\cos ^2 x\right)\right] \\
& +\cos 2 x\left[\left(1-\cos ^2 x\right) \cos ^2 x-\left(2 \cos ^2 x-1\right)^2\right] \\
& \Delta=\left(2 \cos ^2 x-1\right)\left[4 \cos ^4 x+1-4 \cos ^2 x-\cos ^4 x\right] \\
& -\left(1-\cos ^2 x\right)[\cos 2 x(-\cos 2 x)] \\
& +\cos 2 x\left[\cos ^2 x-\cos ^4 x-4 \cos ^4 x-1+4 \cos ^2 x\right] \\
& =\left(2 \cos ^2 x-1\right)\left[3 \cos ^4 x+1+5 \cos ^2 x-5 \cos ^4 x-1\right] \\
& +\left(1-\cos ^2 x\right)\left[ \left(2 \cos ^2 x-1\right)^2\right] \\
& \Rightarrow\left(2 \cos ^2 x-1\right)\left[5 \cos ^2 x-2 \cos ^4 x\right]+\left(2 \cos ^2 x-1\right) \\
& {\left[2 \cos ^2 x-1-2 \cos ^3 x+\cos ^2 x\right]} \\
& \Rightarrow\left(2 \cos ^2 x-1\right)\left[5 \cos ^2 x-2 \cos ^4 x+3 \cos ^2 x\right. \\
& \left.-2 \cos ^3 x-1\right] \\
& \Rightarrow\left(2 \cos ^2 x-1\right)\left[8 \cos ^2 x-2 \cos ^4 x-2 \cos ^3 x-1\right] \\
&
\end{aligned} Hence, constant term will be $(-1) $\times(-1)=1$

8243.text: The differential equation of the family of parabola with focus as the origin and the axis as $X$-axis, is :

8243.sol:
Given that,
Focus $S=(0,0)$, let $P(x, y)$ be any point on the parabola.
Since, $S P^2=P M^2\Rightarrow \quad(x-0)^2+(y-0)^2=(x+a)^2\Rightarrow \quad x^2+y^2=x^2+a^2+2 x a\Rightarrow \quad y^2=2 a x+a^2\ldots$ (i)
$\Rightarrow \quad 2 y \frac{d y}{d x}=2 a\ldots$ (ii)
From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$y^2=2 y \frac{d y}{d x} \cdot x+\left(y \frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2\Rightarrow \quad y^2\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2+2 x y \frac{d y}{d x}=y^2\Rightarrow \quad y\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2+2 x \frac{d y}{d x}=y\therefore \quad-y\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2=2 x \frac{d y}{d x}-y$

8436.text: If $x=3 \cos t$ and $y=4 \sin t$, then $\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}$ at the point $\left(x_0, y_0\right)=\left(\frac{3}{2}$ \sqrt{2}, 2 \sqrt{2}\right), is
8436.sol:
We have,

\begin{aligned}
& x=3 $\cos t \text{$ and } y=4 $\sin t$ \\
& \Rightarrow \quad $\frac{x^2}{9}+\frac{y^2}{16}=$\cos ^2 t+$\sin ^2 t$ \\
& \Rightarrow \quad $\frac{x^2}{9}+\frac{y^2}{16}=$1 \\
& \Rightarrow $\frac{2 x}{9}+\frac{2 y}{16} \frac{d y}{d x}=$0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad $\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{-16}{9} \frac{x}{y}$ \\
& \Rightarrow \quad $\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}=\frac{-16}{9}\left[\frac{1 \cdot y-x $$\frac{d y}{d x}$$}{y^2}\right] \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}=\frac{-16}{9}\left[\frac{y-x-\left(\frac{-16}{9}\frac{x}{y}\right)$}{y^2}\right] \\
& =$\frac{-16}{9}\left[\frac{9 y^2+16 x^2}{9 y^3}\right]=\frac{-16}{9}$ \times $\frac{144}{9 y^3}$$\left[\because $\frac{x^2}{9}$+$\frac{y^2}{16}$=1\right]$$ \\
& =\frac{-16 \times 144}{81 \times(2 \sqrt{2})^3} \quad\left[\because\left(x_0, y_0\right)$=$\left(\frac{3 \sqrt{2}}{2}, 2 \sqrt{2}\right)\right] \\
& =\frac{-16 \times 144}{81 \times 16 \sqrt{2}}=\frac{-144}{81 \times \sqrt{2}}=\frac{-16}{9 \sqrt{2}}=\frac{-8 \sqrt{2}}{9} \\
&
\end{aligned}
$

19770.subject: Chemistry
19770.text: Identify the pair of molecules, both of which have positive values of Dipole moment.
19770.sol:
The dipole moment of a molecule depends on its geometry and the polarity of its bonds. A molecule has a non-zero dipole moment if its bond dipoles do not cancel each other out.

$\mathrm{BF}_3$ has a trigonal planar geometry. The three $\mathrm{B-F}$ bond dipoles are equal and oriented at $120^{{}^{\circ}}$ to each other, resulting in a net dipole moment of zero.

$\mathrm{CCl}_4$ has a tetrahedral geometry. The four $\mathrm{C-Cl}$ bond dipoles are equal and arranged symmetrically, resulting in a net dipole moment of zero.

$\mathrm{NF}_3$ has a trigonal pyramidal geometry with a lone pair on the nitrogen atom. The bond dipoles of the three $\mathrm{N-F}$ bonds and the lone pair do not cancel out, resulting in a net dipole moment of approximately $0.24 \text{ D}$.

$\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ has a tetrahedral geometry, but because the atoms attached to the central carbon are not identical (three $\mathrm{Cl}$ atoms and one $\mathrm{H}$ atom), the bond dipoles do not cancel, resulting in a net dipole moment of approximately $1.01 \text{ D}$.

Comparing the options, both $\mathrm{NF}_3$ and $\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ have non-zero (positive) dipole moments.

Answer: $\mathrm{NF}_3 \mathrm{CHCl}_3$

$ Au^{3+}/Au$: $E° = +1.50$ V > +1.49 V \Rightarrow cannot be oxidised

$ Cr^{3+}/Cr$: $E° = -0.74$ V < +1.49 V \Rightarrow can be oxidised

$ Ag^+/Ag$: $E° = +0.8$ V < +1.49 V \Rightarrow can be oxidised

The two species that cannot be oxidised are (a) and (c).

20217.subject: Chemistry
20217.text: Which one of the following is not the correct IUPAC name of the compound?
20217.sol:
Let us evaluate the IUPAC name for each given structure:

Option (A): The structure is $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{O}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$. The alkyl group attached to the oxygen atom is a 3-methylbutyl group. Thus, the ether is named 3-methylbutoxybenzene. This name is correct.

Option (B): The structure is $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{C}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. The principal functional group is $-\text{OH}$, so the longest chain containing the $-\text{OH}$ group and the double bond is selected and numbered from the right to give the $-\text{OH}$ group the lowest locant (1). The substituents are a bromo group at C-2 and a methyl group at C-3. The name is 2-bromo-3-methylbut-2-en-1-ol. This name is correct.

Option (C): The structure is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_2\text{OH})-\text{CH}_3$. The principal chain must contain both $-\text{OH}$ groups. The longest such chain has 6 carbon atoms. Numbering from right to left gives the $-\text{OH}$ groups the lower locants (1,3) compared to left to right (4,6). The methyl substituents are at C-2 and C-5. The name is 2,5-dimethylhexane-1,3-diol. This name is correct.

Option (D): The structure is a cyclohexane ring with a propoxy group ($-\text{OC}_3\text{H}_7$) and two methyl groups on adjacent carbons. We must number the ring to give the lowest possible locant set for the substituents. Numbering from the carbon with the two methyl groups gives the locant set $1, 1, 2$. Numbering from the carbon with the propoxy group gives the locant set $1, 2, 2$. Comparing the two sets, $1, 1, 2$ is lower than $1, 2, 2$. Therefore, the methyl groups are at position 1 and the propoxy group is at position 2. Alphabetically, 'methyl' comes before 'propoxy'. The correct IUPAC name is 1,1-dimethyl-2-propoxycyclohexane. The given name 2,2-dimethyl-1-propoxycyclohexane is incorrect.

Answer: 2,2–Dimethyl–1–propoxycyclohexane:

Carbon tetrachloride is primarily used as a solvent for oils, fats, lacquers, varnishes, rubber waxes, and resins. It is also used as a fire extinguisher under the name Pyrene. It is not used as a preservative for anatomical specimens; formaldehyde is commonly used for that purpose.

Dichloromethane is widely used as a solvent in the pharmaceutical industry, as a paint remover, as a propellant in aerosols, and as a process solvent in the manufacture of drugs.

Freon-12 (dichlorodifluoromethane) is a chlorofluorocarbon used as a refrigerant and as a propellant in aerosol sprays.

DDT (p,p'-dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane) was widely used as an insecticide to protect crops and to control mosquitoes that spread malaria and lice that carry typhus.

Answer: Carbon tetrachloride is used as a preservative for anatomical specimens

21179.subject: Mathematics
21179.text: If $z=\sqrt{3}+i$, then the argument of $z^2 e^{z-i}$ is equal to
21179.sol:
Given $z = \sqrt{3} + i$.

Express $z$ in polar form: $z = r(\cos \theta + i \sin \theta)$, where $r = |z| = \sqrt{(\sqrt{3})^2 + 1^2} = 2$ and $\theta = \arg(z) = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

Thus, $z = 2e^{i\pi/6}$.

We need to find the argument of $w = z^2 e^{z-i}$.

Taking the argument of both sides: $\arg(w) = \arg(z^2 e^{z-i}) = \arg(z^2) + \arg(e^{z-i})$.

Using properties of arguments: $\arg(z^2) = 2 \arg(z) = 2 \times \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

For the second term, let $z - i = x + iy$. Since $z = \sqrt{3} + i$, $z - i = \sqrt{3} + i - i = \sqrt{3}$.

Therefore, $e^{z-i} = e^{\sqrt{3}}$.

Since $e^{\sqrt{3}}$ is a positive real number, its argument is $0$.

Thus, $\arg(w) = \dfrac{\pi}{3} + 0 = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$

21557.subject: Mathematics
21557.text: $\int \log x(\log x+2) d x $$\text{ equals to }$
21557.sol:
Let $I = \int \log x(\log x + 2) dx$.

Expanding the integrand, we get $I = \int ((\log x)^2 + 2 \log x) dx$.

Consider the function $f(x) = x(\log x)^2$.

Differentiating $f(x)$ with respect to $x$ using the product rule:

$f'(x) = \dfrac{d}{dx}[x] \cdot (\log x)^2 + x \cdot \dfrac{d}{dx}[(\log x)^2]$

$f'(x) = 1 \cdot (\log x)^2 + x \cdot 2 \log x \cdot \dfrac{1}{x}$

$f'(x) = (\log x)^2 + 2 \log x$.

Since the derivative of $x(\log x)^2$ is exactly the integrand, the integral is $x(\log x)^2 + C$.

Answer: $x(\log x)^2+C$

21913.subject: Mathematics
21913.text: What is the probability of a randomly chosen 2 digit number being divisible by 3 ?
21913.sol:
The set of all 2-digit numbers ranges from $10$ to $99$.

The total number of 2-digit numbers is $99 - 10 + 1 = 90$.

The 2-digit numbers divisible by $3$ form an arithmetic progression: $12, 15, 18, \dots, 99$.

Using the formula for the $n$-th term of an arithmetic progression, $a_n = a + (n - 1)d$, where $a = 12$, $d = 3$, and $a_n = 99$:

$99 = 12 + (n - 1)3$

$87 = (n - 1)3$

$29 = n - 1$

$n = 30$.

The probability of choosing a 2-digit number divisible by $3$ is the ratio of the number of favorable outcomes to the total number of outcomes:

$P = \dfrac{30}{90} = \dfrac{1}{3}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{3}$

23141.subject: Physics
23141.text: 64 rain drops of the same radius are falling through air with a steady velocity of $0.5 \mathrm{ cm} \mathrm{ s}^{-1}$. If the drops coalesce, the terminal velocity would be
23141.sol:
Let $r$ be the radius of each small drop and $v$ be its terminal velocity. The terminal velocity of a spherical drop is given by Stokes Law as $v = \dfrac{2}{9} \dfrac{r^2(\rho - \sigma)g}{\eta}$, where $\rho$ is the density of the drop, $\sigma$ is the density of air, and $\eta$ is the coefficient of viscosity. This implies $v \propto r^2$.

When $n = 64$ drops coalesce into a single large drop of radius $R$, the volume remains constant. Thus, $\dfrac{4}{3} \pi R^3 = n \times \dfrac{4}{3} \pi r^3$, which gives $R^3 = n r^3$, or $R = n^{1/3} r$.

Substituting $n = 64$, we get $R = (64)^{1/3} r = 4r$.

Let $V$ be the terminal velocity of the large drop. Since $V \propto R^2$ and $v \propto r^2$, we have $\dfrac{V}{v} = \left( \dfrac{R}{r} \right)^2 = (4)^2 = 16$.

Given $v = 0.5 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$, the terminal velocity of the large drop is $V = 16 \times 0.5 \text{ cm s}^{-1} = 8 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$.

Converting to meters per second, $V = 8 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m s}^{-1} = 0.08 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Answer: $0.08 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$

23285.subject: Physics
23285.text: Which of the following technique is not used for measuring small time intervals?
23285.sol:
Time measurement techniques are classified based on the physical phenomena involved. Electronic oscillators, such as quartz crystal oscillators, are used for precise timekeeping in electronic devices. Atomic clocks utilize the vibrations of atoms, such as cesium-133, to measure time with extreme precision. The decay of elementary particles is a fundamental process used in particle physics to measure extremely short time intervals. A spring oscillator, while periodic, is subject to significant damping, friction, and environmental factors, making it unsuitable for the precise measurement of small time intervals compared to the other high-precision methods listed.

Answer: Spring oscillator

25196.text: Which is correct statement if $\mathrm{N}_2$ is added at equilibrium condition?
options:
The equilibrium will shift to forward direction because according to IInd law of thermodynamics the entropy must increases in the direction of spontaneous reaction.

The condition for equilibrium is $G_{\mathrm{N}_2}+3 G_{\mathrm{H}_2}=2 G_{\mathrm{NH}_3}$ where $G$ is Gibbs free energy per mole of the gaseous species measured at the partial pressure. The condition of equilibrium is unaffected by the use of catalyst, which increases the rate of both the forward and backward reactions to the same extent.

The catalyst will increase the rate of forward reaction by $\alpha$ and that of backward reaction by $\beta$.

Catalyst will not alter the rate of either of the reaction.
25196.sol: $K_p or K_c$ remains constant for above reaction at constant temperature. Although in presence of catalyst rate of forward and backward reaction is increased in same order (extent) due to decreasing the activation energy of both reaction. So the equilibrium is established in short time i.e., catalyst is able to increase the concentration of reactants and products in same order, so the value of $K_C or K_p$ remains constant. Hence equilibrium state is not effected in presence of catalyst. Hence, at equilibrium $\Delta G=0 \begin{aligned}& \because \quad \Delta G=2 G \text{$ of $} \mathrm{NH}_{3}-\left(\mathrm{G} \text{ of } \mathrm{H}_{2}+3 \times G \text{ of } \mathrm{NH} }_{3}\right) \\ & \therefore G_{\mathrm{N}_2}+3 G_{\mathrm{H}_2}=2 G_{\mathrm{NH}_3} \end{aligned}$

25274.text:
Let the functions $f: R \to R$ and $g: R \to R$ be defined by
$f\left(x\right) = {e}^{x - 1} - {e}^{- \left|x - 1\right|}$ and $g\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left({e}^{x - 1} + {e}^{1 - x}\right)$.
Then the area of the region in the first quadrant bounded by the curves $y = f\left(x\right), y = g\left(x\right)$ and $x = 0$ is
25274.sol:
$f\left(x\right) = {e}^{x - 1} - {e}^{- \left|x - 1\right|} = \left\{\begin{cases}0, & x \le 1 \\ {e}^{x - 1} - {e}^{1 - x}, & x > 1\end{cases}\right) and

$g\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left({e}^{x - 1} + {e}^{1 - x}\right)$

At $x = 0, f\left(0\right) = 0 & g\left(0\right) = \dfrac{e + {e}^{- 1}}{2}$

At $x = 1, f\left(1\right) = 0 & g\left(1\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left({e}^{1 - 1} + {e}^{1 - 1}\right) = 1$

For point of intersection of the two curves for $x > 1$, $f\left(x\right) = g\left(x\right)$

$⇒ {e}^{x - 1} - {e}^{1 - x} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left({e}^{x - 1} + {e}^{1 - x}\right)$

$⇒ 2{e}^{x - 1} - 2{e}^{1 - x} = {e}^{x - 1} + {e}^{1 - x}$

$⇒ {e}^{x - 1} = 3{e}^{1 - x}$

$⇒ {\left({e}^{x - 1}\right)}^{2} = 3$

$⇒ x = 1 + ln\sqrt{3}$

$∴$Required area $=$ Area of the shaded region

$= {∫}_{0}^{1}g\left(x\right)dx + {∫}_{1}^{1 + ln\sqrt{3}}\left\{g\left(x\right) - f\left(x\right)\right\}dx$

$= {∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{2}\left({e}^{x - 1} + {e}^{1 - x}\right)dx + {∫}_{1}^{1 + ln\sqrt{3}}\left\{\dfrac{1}{2}\left({e}^{x - 1} + {e}^{1 - x}\right) - \left({e}^{x - 1} - {e}^{1 - x}\right)\right\}dx$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}\left({e}^{x - 1} + {e}^{1 - x}\right)dx + \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{1}^{1 + ln\sqrt{3}}\left(3{e}^{1 - x} - {e}^{x - 1}\right)dx$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}{\left[{e}^{x - 1} - {e}^{1 - x}\right]}_{0}^{1} - \dfrac{1}{2}{\left[3{e}^{1 - x} + {e}^{x - 1}\right]}_{1}^{1 + ln\sqrt{3}}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(e - {e}^{- 1}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[2\sqrt{3} - 4\right]$

$= \dfrac{e - {e}^{- 1}}{2} + \left(2 - \sqrt{3}\right)$

25381.text: Let $g: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function with $g\left(0\right) = 0, {g}^{′}\left(0\right) = 0 and {g}^{′}\left(1\right) \ne 0 .$ Let $f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}\dfrac{x}{| x |}g\left(x\right), & x \ne 0 \\ 0, & x = 0\end{cases}\right) and $h\left(x\right) = {e}^{| x |}$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R} .$ Let $\left(foh\right) ( x )$ denote $f\left(h\left(x\right)\right)and ( hof ) ( x )$denote $h\left(f\left(x\right)\right)$ .Then which of the following is (are) true?
25381.sol:
$f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}g\left(x\right) & x > 0 \\ 0 & x = 0 \\ - g\left(x\right) & x < 0\end{cases}\right)
$LHD: \lim_{x \to {0}^{-}} ⁡ \left(- {g}^{′}\left(x\right)\right) = - \lim_{x \to {0}^{-}} ⁡ {g}^{′}\left(x\right) = - 0 = 0$
$RHD: \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}} ⁡ {g}^{′}\left(x\right) = {g}^{′}\left({0}^{+}\right) = 0$
Hence $f\left(x\right)$ is differentiable at $x = 0$
$h\left(x\right) = {e}^{\left|x\right|} = \left\{\begin{cases}{e}^{x} & x \ge 0 \\ {e}^{- x} & x < 0\end{cases}\right)
$LHD: \lim_{x \to {0}^{-}} ⁡ \left(- {e}^{- x}\right) = - 1$
$RHD: \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}} ⁡ \left({e}^{x}\right) = 1$
Hence $h\left(x\right)$ is not differentiable at $x = 0$
$f\left(h\left(x\right)\right) = \left\{\dfrac{{e}^{\left|x\right|}}{\left|{e}^{\left|x\right|}\right|}\rightg\left({e}^{\left|x\right|}\right)$
$f\left(h\left(x\right)\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}g\left({e}^{x}\right) & x \ge 0 \\ g\left({e}^{- x}\right) & x < 0\end{cases}\right)
$LHD: \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}} ⁡ {g}^{′}\left({e}^{- x}\right) \times - {e}^{- x} = {g}^{′}\left(1\right) \times - 1 = - {g}^{′}\left(1\right)$
$RHD: \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}} ⁡ {g}^{′}\left({e}^{x}\right) \times{e}^{x} = {g}^{′}\left(1\right)$
Hence foh is non-differentiable at $x = 0$
$h\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}1 & x = 0 \\ {e}^{\left|\dfrac{x}{\left|x\right|}g\left(x\right)\right|} & x \ne 0\end{cases}\right)
$= \left\{\begin{cases}1 & x = 0 \\ {e}^{\left|g\left(x\right)\right|} & x \ne 0\end{cases}\right)
$LHD: \lim_{x \to {0}^{-}} ⁡ {e}^{\left|g\left(x\right)\right|} \times \pm {g}^{′}\left(x\right) = {e}^{\left|g\left({0}^{-}\right)\right|} \times \pm \left({g}^{′}\left({0}^{-}\right)\right) = 0$
$RHD: \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}} ⁡ {e}^{\left|g\left(x\right)\right|} \times \pm {g}^{′}\left(x\right) = {e}^{\left|g\left({0}^{+}\right)\right|} \times \pm {g}^{′}\left({0}^{+}\right) = 0$

26188.subject: Physics
26188.text: An electric dipole is formed by two charges $+ q$ and $- q$ located in $xy$-plane at $( 0, 2 ) mm$ and $( 0, - 2 ) mm$, respectively, as shown in the figure. The electric potential at point $P ( 100, 100 ) mm$ due to the dipole is ${V}_{0}$. The charges $+ q$ and $– q$ are then moved to the points $( - 1, 2 ) mm$ and $( 1, - 2 ) mm$, respectively. What is the value of electric potential at $P$ due to the new dipole?
26188.sol:
Electric potential at any general point for vertical dipole is written as, ${V}_{1} ∝ \dfrac{{p}_{1}cos{\theta}_{1}}{{\left({r}_{1}\right)}^{2}}$.

Electric potential at any general point for ${V}_{2} ∝ \dfrac{{p}_{2}cos{\theta}_{2}}{{\left({r}_{2}\right)}^{2}}$.

For first case:

$tan{\theta}_{1} = \dfrac{100}{100} = 1 ⇒ {\theta}_{1} = 45 °$

For second case:

slope in this is $= \dfrac{- 2 - 2}{1 - \left(- 1\right)} = - 2$

which is equal to

$tan\left(45 ° + {\theta}_{2}\right) = - 2 ⇒ \dfrac{1 + tan{\theta}_{2}}{1 - tan{\theta}_{2}} = - 2 ⇒ 1 + tan{\theta}_{2} = - 2 + 2tan{\theta}_{2} ⇒ tan{\theta}_{2} = 3cos{\theta}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{{3}^{2} + {1}^{2}}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10}}$

also ${r}_{1} = {r}_{2}$.

Therefore, required ratio

$\dfrac{{V}_{2}}{{V}_{1}} = \dfrac{{p}_{2}cos{\theta}_{2}}{{p}_{1}cos{\theta}_{1}}$

$\dfrac{{V}_{2}}{{V}_{1}} = \dfrac{q{l}_{2} \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10}}}{q{l}_{1} \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{{\left(2 - \left(- 2\right)\right)}^{2} + {\left(- 1 - 1\right)}^{2}}}{4 \times \sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{5}}{4 \times \sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ {V}_{2} = \dfrac{{V}_{0}}{2}$

27782.subject: Chemistry
27782.text: The total number of anti bonding molecular orbitals, formed from $2s$ and $2p$ atomic orbitals in a diatomic molecule is _____________.
27782.sol:
The atomic orbitals combine to form a new set of equivalent orbitals known as hybrid orbitals. Unlike pure orbitals, hybrid orbitals are used in bond formation. The phenomenon is known as hybridisation, which can be defined as the process of intermixing of the orbitals of slightly different energies to redistribute their energies, resulting in the formation of a new set of orbitals of equivalent energies and shape.

The number of hybrid orbitals is equal to the number of atomic orbitals that get hybridised.

Antibonding molecular orbital from $2s = 1$ that is $\sigma * 2s$

Antibonding molecular orbital from $2p = 3$ that is $\sigma * 2{p}_{x}, \pi * 2{p}_{y}and\pi * 2{p}_{z}$.

Total $= 4$

29559.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason $( R )$
Assertion (A) : Photochemical smog causes cracking of rubber.
Reason (R): Presence of ozone, nitric oxide, acrolein, formaldehyde and peroxyacetyl nitrate in photochemical smog makes it oxidizing.
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: $( A )$ is false but $( R )$ is true.
Both $( A )$ and $( R )$ are true but $( R )$ is not the true explanation of $( A )$.
Both $( A )$ and $( R )$ are true and $( R )$ is the true explanation of $( A )$.
(A) is true but $( R )$ is false.
29559.sol:
Photochemical smog has high concentration of oxidising agents and is, therefore, called as oxidising smog.
The common components of photochemical smog are ozone, nitric oxide, acrolein, formaldehyde and peroxyacetyl nitrate (PAN). Photochemical smog causes serious health problems. Both ozone and PAN act as powerful eye irritants. Ozone and nitric oxide irritate the nose and throat and their high concentration causes headache, chest pain, dryness of the throat, cough and difficulty in breathing. Photochemical smog leads to cracking of rubber and extensive damage to plant life. It also causes corrosion of metals, stones, building materials, rubber and painted surfaces.

34440.sol:
Coefficient matrix determinant: $\Delta = 1(15-2a) - 1(6-a) + 1(4-5) = 8 - a$.
For $a = 8$, $\Delta = 0$, so unique solution is not possible.
With $a = 8$: $R_2 - 2R_1$ gives $3y + 6z = 24 \Rightarrow y + 2z = 8$.
$R_3 - R_1$ gives $y + 2z = b - 6$.
For consistency: $b - 6 = 8 \Rightarrow b = 14$.
When $a = 8, b = 14$: the system has infinitely many solutions.

With $\vec{AP} = (39, α, β+1)$, the cross product gives $\vec{AP} \times \vec{d} = (3α, 2β - 115, -2α)$.
Thus $|\vec{AP} \times \vec{d}| = \sqrt{13α^2 + (2β - 115)^2}$ and $|\vec{d}| = \sqrt{13}$.
Setting $\frac{\sqrt{13α^2 + (2β - 115)^2}}{\sqrt{13}} = 13\sqrt{10}$ gives $α^2 + \frac{(2β - 115)^2}{13} = 1690$.
Solving with the constraint β < 0: α = 5, β = -13, hence $α^2 + β^2 = 25 + 169 = 170$.

40883.text: A body of mass is taken from earth surface to the height $h$ equal to twice the radius of earth $( {R}_{e} )$, the increase in potential energy will be : ($g =$ acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth)
40883.sol:
The potential energy of a particle at a distance $r ( > {R}_{e} )$ from the centre of Earth is,

$U = - G\dfrac{{M}_{e}m}{r}$

Initially, the particle is at a height ${R}_{e}$ from the surface. Therefore, $r = {R}_{e}$.

$∴ {U}_{i} = - G\dfrac{{M}_{e}m}{{R}_{e}}$

When height is increased to $2{R}_{e}$ from surface, $r = 2{R}_{e} + {R}_{e} = 3{R}_{e}$

$∴ {U}_{f} = - G\dfrac{{M}_{e}m}{3{R}_{e}}$

Thus, the change in potential energy is

$∆ U = {U}_{f} - {U}_{i} = - G\dfrac{{M}_{e}m}{3{R}_{e}} + G\dfrac{{M}_{e}m}{{R}_{e}} = \dfrac{2}{3}G\dfrac{{M}_{e}m}{{R}_{e}} = \dfrac{2}{3}G\dfrac{{M}_{e}}{{{R}_{e}}^{2}}m{R}_{e} = \dfrac{2}{3}mg{R}_{e}\left(\text{as}g = G\dfrac{{M}_{e}}{{{R}_{e}}^{2}}\right)$

41282.text: One end of a massless spring of spring constant $k$ and natural length ${l}_{0}$ is fixed while the other end is connected to a small object of mass $m$ lying on a frictionless table. $⇒ \left(k - m{\omega}^{2}\right)x = m{\omega}^{2}{l}_{0}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{m{\omega}^{2}{l}_{0}}{k - m{\omega}^{2}}$

44190.subject: Physics
44190.text: An unpolarized light of intensity $I_o$ passes through polarizer and then through a certain optically active solution and finally it goes to analyser. If the angle between analyser and polariser is $0°$ and intensity of light emerged from analyser is $\dfrac{3}{8}I_o$, the angle of rotation of the light by the solution with respect to analyser is _______ degrees.
44190.sol:
Intensity of light after passing through the first polarizer is:

$I_1 = \dfrac{I_o}{2}$

Let the optically active solution rotate the plane of polarization by an angle $\theta$. Since the angle between the polarizer and the analyser is $0^\circ$, the angle between the plane of polarization of the light emerging from the solution and the transmission axis of the analyser is also $\theta$.

According to Malus's law, the intensity of light emerging from the analyser is:

$I_2 = I_1 \cos^2 \theta = \dfrac{I_o}{2} \cos^2 \theta$

Given that the final intensity is $\dfrac{3}{8}I_o$, we have:

$\dfrac{I_o}{2} \cos^2 \theta = \dfrac{3}{8}I_o$

$\cos^2 \theta = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$\cos \theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$\theta = 30^\circ$

Answer: $30$

46370.text: If ratio of terminal velocity of two drops falling in air is $3: 4$, then what is the ratio of their surface area?
46370.sol:
Terminal velocity is given by $v=\frac{2 r^2(\rho-\sigma)}{9 \eta} g$
where, $r=$ radius of drop,
$\rho=$ density of medium of drop,
$\sigma=$ density of surrounding medium
$\eta=$ coefficient of viscocity of drop medium.
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{v} \propto \mathrm{r}^2$, we know area of drop $\propto \mathrm{r}^2$
$\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{v} \propto \mathrm{A}$ (area) $\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{v}_1}{\mathrm{v}_2}=\frac{\mathrm{A}_1}{\mathrm{~A}_2}=\frac{3}{4}$
$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\mathrm{A}_1}{\mathrm{~A}_2}=\frac{3}{4}$

49198.text: In Linear Programming Problem (LPP), the objective function $Z = ax + by$ has the same maximum value at two corner points. The number of points at which $Z_\max$ occurs is
49198.sol:
According to the Fundamental Theorem of Linear Programming, if the optimal value of the objective function occurs at two distinct corner points of the feasible region, it also occurs at all points on the line segment joining these two points.

Since a line segment contains an infinite number of points, the maximum value $Z_\max$ occurs at infinitely many points.

Answer: Infinity

Then, $h=-\frac{f\left(x_0\right)}{f\left(x_0\right)}=-\frac{f(2)}{f(2)}\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & h=-\left[\frac{(2)^4-2-10}{4(2)^3-1}\right] \\ \Rightarrow & h=-\left[\frac{16-12}{31}\right]=\frac{-4}{31} \\ \Rightarrow & h=-0.129\end{array}
\therefore$ Positive square root of $f(x)$ by Newton-Raphson method,
$\begin{aligned} x_1=x_0+h & =2+(-0.129) \\ & =2-0.129=1.871\end{aligned}$

In a reaction,

57572.text:
What is the product P obtained in following reaction?
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{AgCN}_{(alc)} \rightarrow \text{P}$
57572.sol:
$\text{AgCN}$ is predominantly a covalent compound. The bond between $\text{Ag}$ and $\text{C}$ is covalent, which leaves the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom available for nucleophilic attack.

When an alkyl halide such as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ reacts with alcoholic $\text{AgCN}$, the nucleophilic attack occurs through the nitrogen atom rather than the carbon atom.

This results in the formation of an alkyl isocyanide as the major product.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{AgCN}_{(alc)} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NC} + \text{AgBr}$

The product P is ethyl isocyanide, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NC}$.

59924.subject: Chemistry
59924.text: Identify from following the correct set of thermodynamic conditions for the reaction to be spontaneous below equilibrium temperature.
59924.sol:
The spontaneity of a reaction is determined by the Gibbs free energy: $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$, with $\Delta G < 0$ indicating spontaneity. At equilibrium, $\Delta G = 0$, so $T_{\text{eq}} = \frac{\Delta H}{\Delta S}$.

For $\Delta H < 0$ and $\Delta S < 0$, $\Delta G$ becomes less negative as temperature increases. Spontaneity requires $|\Delta H| > T|\Delta S|$, equivalent to $T < \frac{|\Delta H|}{|\Delta S|} = T_{\text{eq}}$, confirming the reaction is spontaneous below the equilibrium temperature.

Other combinations yield different behavior: $\Delta H > 0$, $\Delta S > 0$ gives spontaneity above $T_{\text{eq}}$; $\Delta H < 0$, $\Delta S > 0$ is always spontaneous; $\Delta H > 0$, $\Delta S < 0$ is never spontaneous.

The conditions $\Delta H < 0$ and $\Delta S < 0$ correspond to option A.

60212.subject: Mathematics
60212.text: A spherical mothball has initial radius 3 cm. Due to evaporation, the radius of the ball reduces to 1 cm in 4 months. In how many months would the mothball evaporate completely if the volume is lost at a rate proportional to the surface area ?
60212.sol:
Let $V$ be the volume and $S$ be the surface area of the spherical mothball of radius $r$.

$V = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi r^3$

$S = 4 \pi r^2$

Given that the rate of loss of volume is proportional to the surface area:

$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = -k S$

Differentiating $V$ with respect to $t$:

$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt} \left( \dfrac{4}{3} \pi r^3 \right) = 4 \pi r^2 \dfrac{dr}{dt} = S \dfrac{dr}{dt}$

Equating the two expressions for $\dfrac{dV}{dt}$:

$S \dfrac{dr}{dt} = -k S \Rightarrow \dfrac{dr}{dt} = -k$

Integrating both sides with respect to $t$:

$r(t) = -kt + C$

At $t = 0$, $r = 3$ cm, which gives $C = 3$.

$r(t) = 3 - kt$

At $t = 4$ months, $r = 1$ cm:

$1 = 3 - 4k \Rightarrow 4k = 2 \Rightarrow k = \dfrac{1}{2}$

The mothball evaporates completely when $r(t) = 0$:

$0 = 3 - \dfrac{1}{2} t \Rightarrow t = 6$ months.

Answer: $6$ months

61631.subject: Mathematics
61631.text: The derivative of $f(\sin x)$ with respect to $g(\sec x)$ at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, given that $f'\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = 3$ and $g'(\sqrt{2}) = 1$ is.....
61631.sol:
Let $u = f(\sin x)$ and $v = g(\sec x)$

$\dfrac{du}{dx} = f'(\sin x) \cos x$

$\dfrac{dv}{dx} = g'(\sec x) \sec x \tan x$

$\dfrac{du}{dv} = \dfrac{\dfrac{du}{dx}}{\dfrac{dv}{dx}} = \dfrac{f'(\sin x) \cos x}{g'(\sec x) \sec x \tan x}$

At $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$:

$\dfrac{du}{dv} = \dfrac{f'\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) \cdot \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}{g'(\sqrt{2}) \cdot \sqrt{2} \cdot 1}$

Substituting $f'\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = 3$ and $g'(\sqrt{2}) = 1$:

$\dfrac{du}{dv} = \dfrac{3 \cdot \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}{1 \cdot \sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{2}$

61660.sol:
Given $y^{\dfrac{1}{m}} + y^{-\dfrac{1}{m}} = 2x$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{1}{m} y^{\dfrac{1}{m} - 1} y_1 - \dfrac{1}{m} y^{-\dfrac{1}{m} - 1} y_1 = 2$

$\dfrac{y_1}{m y} \left( y^{\dfrac{1}{m}} - y^{-\dfrac{1}{m}} \right) = 2$

$y_1 \left( y^{\dfrac{1}{m}} - y^{-\dfrac{1}{m}} \right) = 2my$

Squaring both sides:

$y_1^2 \left( y^{\dfrac{1}{m}} - y^{-\dfrac{1}{m}} \right)^2 = 4m^2 y^2$

Using the identity $(a - b)^2 = (a + b)^2 - 4ab$:

$y_1^2 \left[ \left( y^{\dfrac{1}{m}} + y^{-\dfrac{1}{m}} \right)^2 - 4 \right] = 4m^2 y^2$

Substituting $y^{\dfrac{1}{m}} + y^{-\dfrac{1}{m}} = 2x$:

$y_1^2 \left[ (2x)^2 - 4 \right] = 4m^2 y^2$

$y_1^2 (4x^2 - 4) = 4m^2 y^2$

$4(x^2 - 1)y_1^2 = 4m^2 y^2$

$(x^2 - 1)y_1^2 = m^2 y^2$

Answer: $m^2 y^2$

64202.text: If $A(2,-3)$ and $C(-6,7)$ are opposite vertices of a rhombus ABCD, then the equation of diagonal BD is
64202.sol:
The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles. Thus, diagonal $BD$ is the perpendicular bisector of diagonal $AC$.

The midpoint of diagonal $AC$ is $\left(\dfrac{2 - 6}{2}, \dfrac{-3 + 7}{2}\right) = (-2, 2)$.

The slope of diagonal $AC$ is $m_{AC} = \dfrac{7 - (-3)}{-6 - 2} = \dfrac{10}{-8} = -\dfrac{5}{4}$.

Since $BD \perp AC$, the slope of diagonal $BD$ is $m_{BD} = -\dfrac{1}{m_{AC}} = \dfrac{4}{5}$.

The equation of diagonal $BD$, which passes through the midpoint $(-2, 2)$ with slope $\dfrac{4}{5}$, is:

$y - 2 = \dfrac{4}{5}(x - (-2))$

$5(y - 2) = 4(x + 2)$

$5y - 10 = 4x + 8$

$4x - 5y + 18 = 0$

64454.text: If the angle between the line $x=\frac{\mathrm{y}-1}{2}=\frac{\mathrm{z}-3}{\lambda}$ and the plane $x+2 y+3 z=4$ is $\cos ^{-1} \sqrt{\frac{5}{14}}$, then the value of $\lambda$ is
64454.sol:
The line $L$ has direction vector $\vec{d} = (1, 2, \lambda)$ and the plane $P: x + 2y + 3z = 4$ has normal vector $\vec{n} = (1, 2, 3)$.

The given angle between the line and plane is $\cos^{-1} \sqrt{\frac{5}{14}}$, so $\cos\theta = \sqrt{\frac{5}{14}}$ and $\sin^2\theta = 1 - \cos^2\theta = \frac{9}{14}$, yielding $\sin\theta = \frac{3}{\sqrt{14}}$.

Using the angle formula $\sin\theta = \frac{|\vec{d} \cdot \vec{n}|}{\|\vec{d}\|\|\vec{n}\|}$, we have $\vec{d} \cdot \vec{n} = 5 + 3\lambda$, $\|\vec{d}\| = \sqrt{5 + \lambda^2}$, and $\|\vec{n}\| = \sqrt{14}$.

Substituting gives $\frac{3}{\sqrt{14}} = \frac{|5 + 3\lambda|}{\sqrt{5 + \lambda^2} \cdot \sqrt{14}}$, which simplifies to $3 = \frac{|5 + 3\lambda|}{\sqrt{5 + \lambda^2}}$.

Squaring both sides yields $9 = \frac{(5 + 3\lambda)^2}{5 + \lambda^2}$, and solving the resulting equation gives $\lambda = \frac{20}{30} = \frac{2}{3}$.

Final answer: $\boxed{C}$

65097.text: If $\bar{a} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}$, $\bar{b} = \hat{i} + 3\hat{k}$ and $\bar{c}$ is a unit vector, then the maximum value of the scalar triple product $[\bar{a}\ \bar{b}\ \bar{c}]$ is
65097.sol:
The scalar triple product is given by $[\bar{a}\ \bar{b}\ \bar{c}] = (\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \cdot \bar{c}$.

First, calculating the cross product $\bar{a} \times \bar{b}$:

$\bar{a} \times \bar{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} \text{ and } \hat{j} \text{ and } \hat{k} \\ 2 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } -1 \\ 1 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 3 \end{vmatrix}$

$= \hat{i}(3 - 0) - \hat{j}(6 - (-1)) + \hat{k}(0 - 1)$

$= 3\hat{i} - 7\hat{j} - \hat{k}$

The scalar triple product becomes $(3\hat{i} - 7\hat{j} - \hat{k}) \cdot \bar{c}$.

Using the dot product formula, $(\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \cdot \bar{c} = |\bar{a} \times \bar{b}| |\bar{c}| \cos \theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between $\bar{a} \times \bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$.

Since $\bar{c}$ is a unit vector, $|\bar{c}| = 1$. The maximum value occurs when $\cos \theta = 1$ (i.e., when $\bar{c}$ is parallel to $\bar{a} \times \bar{b}$).

Maximum value $= |\bar{a} \times \bar{b}|$

$= \sqrt{3^2 + (-7)^2 + (-1)^2}$

$= \sqrt{9 + 49 + 1} = \sqrt{59}$

Answer: $\sqrt{59}$

65181.text: The value of $m \in \mathbb{R}$, when angle between the vectors $\bar{p}=m y \hat{i}-6 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k}$ and $\bar{q}=y \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+2 m y \hat{k}$ is obtuse angle, is
65181.sol:
To ensure the angle between vectors $\bar{p}=my\hat{i}-6\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ and $\bar{q}=y\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2my\hat{k}$ is obtuse, the dot product must satisfy $\bar{p} \cdot \bar{q} < 0$. This gives:

$my^2 + 6my - 12 < 0$

For this quadratic inequality to hold for all real $y$, the coefficient of $y^2$ must be negative and the discriminant must be negative.
$m < 0$ is required, and the discriminant $D = (6m)^2 - 4(m)(-12) = 36m^2 + 48m$ satisfies $36m^2 + 48m < 0$.
Factoring gives $12m(3m + 4) < 0$, which holds for $-4/3 < m < 0$.

Combining both conditions yields the range $-4/3 < m < 0$.

The correct option is D.

65573.text: An alternating e.m.f. is given by $e = e_0 \sin \omega t$. In what time the e.m.f. will have half its maximum value, if 'e' starts from zero? (\sin 30^{}^{\circ} = 0.5$)$

$\sin \omega t = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\omega t = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

Substituting $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$:

$\dfrac{2\pi}{T} t = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$t = \dfrac{T}{12}$

Answer: $\dfrac{T}{12}$

& =\mathrm{mg}\left[1-\frac{\sigma_2 \mathrm{~V}}{\mathrm{~m}}\right] \\
& =\mathrm{mg}\left[1-\frac{\sigma_2 \mathrm{~V}}{\sigma_1 \mathrm{~V}}\right] \\

68938.text: A thin glass prism has refractive index $1.5$. The correct relation between the angle of minimum deviation $(\delta m)$ and angle of refraction $(r)$ is
68938.sol:
For a thin prism, the angle of minimum deviation is given by $\delta_m = (\mu - 1)A$.

At the position of minimum deviation, the angle of refraction $r$ inside the prism is $r = \dfrac{A}{2}$, which gives $A = 2r$.

Given the refractive index $\mu = 1.5$.

Substituting the values into the deviation formula, we get:

$\delta_m = (1.5 - 1)(2r)$

$\delta_m = 0.5 \times 2r$

$\delta_m = r$

Answer: $\delta m = r$

70172.subject: Physics
70172.text: In Young's double slit experiment, the separation between the slits is halved and the distance between the slits and the screen is doubled. The fringe width
70172.sol:
The fringe width in Young's double-slit experiment is determined by the relation $\beta = \frac{\lambda D}{d}$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength, $D$ is the slit-to-screen distance, and $d$ is the slit separation.

When the slit separation is halved (d' = d/2$) and the screen distance doubled (D' = 2D$), the new fringe width becomes:

$\beta' = \frac{\lambda D'}{d'} = \frac{\lambda (2D)}{d/2} = \frac{2\lambda D}{d/2} = 4\frac{\lambda D}{d} = 4\beta$

The fringe width thus increases by a factor of four.

Answer: D

70925.subject: Biology
70925.text: Which group has more diversity of known species of organisms from the following?
70925.sol:
According to global biodiversity estimates, animals are the most diverse group of organisms, constituting more than $70\%$ of all recorded species.

Plants (including algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes, gymnosperms, and angiosperms) comprise no more than $22\%$ of the total species.

Among animals, insects are the most species-rich taxonomic group, making up more than $70\%$ of the total animal species.

Therefore, animals have the highest diversity of known species among the given groups.

Answer: Animals

71759.subject: Chemistry
71759.text: Which of the following types of cells is used for electroplating?
71759.sol:
Electroplating is a process that uses electrical energy to drive a non-spontaneous chemical reaction, specifically the deposition of a layer of metal onto a surface.

This process takes place in an electrolytic cell, where an external source of direct current is applied to cause the oxidation and reduction reactions at the electrodes.

Mercury batteries, Leclanche' cells, and fuel cells are galvanic (or voltaic) cells, which generate electrical energy from spontaneous chemical reactions.

Answer: Electrolytic cell

71808.text: What is IUPAC name of acrylic acid?
71808.sol:
The chemical formula of acrylic acid is $CH_2=CH-COOH$.

The principal functional group is the carboxylic acid group ($-COOH$), so numbering starts from the carboxyl carbon.

The longest carbon chain contains $3$ carbon atoms, giving the root word 'prop'.

A double bond is present between $C_2$ and $C_3$, which is indicated by '2-en'.

The secondary suffix for the carboxylic acid is 'oic acid'.

Combining these parts, the IUPAC name is Prop-2-enoic acid.

Answer: Prop-2-enoic acid

71894.subject: Chemistry
71894.text: Identify from following an example of Lewis acid.
71894.sol:
A Lewis acid is a chemical species that can accept a pair of electrons.

In boron trifluoride ($\text{BF}_3$), the central boron atom has only six electrons in its valence shell, making it an electron-deficient molecule.

Due to this incomplete octet, $\text{BF}_3$ can accept an electron pair to complete its octet, thus acting as a Lewis acid.

$\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, $\text{HClO}_4$, and $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ are Bronsted-Lowry acids as they donate protons ($\text{H}^+$).

Answer: $\text{BF}_3$

72224.subject: Physics
72224.text:
Three point charges $+4e$ , $+2e$ and $+e$ are kept at each vertex of an equilateral triangle ABC , each of side $a$. The net electric intensity acting on charge $+e$ is
(\cos 60^{}^{\circ} = 1/2$ and $k$ is constant )$
72224.sol:
Let the charge $+e$ be placed at vertex C of the equilateral triangle ABC, while $+4e$ and $+2e$ are placed at vertices A and B respectively.

The electric intensity (electric field) at C due to the charge $+4e$ at A is:
$E_1 = \dfrac{k(4e)}{a^2}$

The electric intensity at C due to the charge $+2e$ at B is:
$E_2 = \dfrac{k(2e)}{a^2}$

Since ABC is an equilateral triangle, the angle between the electric field vectors $\vec{E}_1$ and $\vec{E}_2$ is $60^{}^{\circ}$.

The net electric intensity at C is given by the vector sum of $\vec{E}_1$ and $\vec{E}_2$:
$E_{net} = \sqrt{E_1^2 + E_2^2 + 2E_1 E_2 \cos 60^{}^{\circ}}$

Substituting the values of $E_1$, $E_2$, and $\cos 60^{}^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{2}$:
$E_{net} = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{4ke}{a^2}\right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{2ke}{a^2}\right)^2 + 2\left(\dfrac{4ke}{a^2}\right)\left(\dfrac{2ke}{a^2}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}$

$E_{net} = \dfrac{ke}{a^2} \sqrt{16 + 4 + 8}$

$E_{net} = \dfrac{ke}{a^2} \sqrt{28}$

$E_{net} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{7}\,ke}{a^2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2\sqrt{7}\,ke}{a^2}$

72333.text: The phase of a particle performing a linear S.H.M increases by $\dfrac{\pi^c}{6} after every 5 second. The frequency of its oscillation is$
72333.sol:
The phase of a particle in S.H.M is given by $\phi = \omega t + \phi_0$

The change in phase over a time interval $\Delta t$ is $\Delta \phi = \omega \Delta t$

Given $\Delta \phi = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$ and $\Delta t = 5 \text{ s}$

$\omega \times 5 = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$\omega = \dfrac{\pi}{30} \text{ rad/s}$

The frequency of oscillation $f$ is given by $f = \dfrac{\omega}{2\pi}$

$f = \dfrac{\pi/30}{2\pi} = \dfrac{1}{60} \text{ Hz}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{60}\text{Hz}$

72480.subject: Physics
72480.text:
Two sources of sound placed closed to each other, are emitting progressive waves given by
$y_1 = 4\sin(600\pi t)$ and $y_2 = 5\sin(608\pi t)$.
An observer located near these two sources of sound will hear
options: $4$ beats/s with intensity ratio $25 : 16$ between waxing and waning.
$8$ beats/s with intensity ratio $25 : 16$ between waxing and waning.
$8$ beats/s with intensity ratio $81 : 1$ between waxing and waning.
$4$ beats/s with intensity ratio $81 : 1$ between waxing and waning.
72480.sol:
The given equations of the progressive waves are:
$y_1 = 4\sin(600\pi t)$
$y_2 = 5\sin(608\pi t)$

Comparing these with the standard equation $y = A\sin(\omega t)$, we get the angular frequencies:
$\omega_1 = 600\pi \Rightarrow 2\pi f_1 = 600\pi \Rightarrow f_1 = 300$ Hz
$\omega_2 = 608\pi \Rightarrow 2\pi f_2 = 608\pi \Rightarrow f_2 = 304$ Hz

The beat frequency is the difference between the frequencies of the two waves:
$n = |f_1 - f_2| = |300 - 304| = 4$ beats/s

The amplitudes of the two waves are $A_1 = 4$ and $A_2 = 5$.
The maximum amplitude during waxing is $A_\max = A_1 + A_2 = 4 + 5 = 9$.
The minimum amplitude during waning is $A_\min = |A_1 - A_2| = |4 - 5| = 1$.

Since intensity is proportional to the square of the amplitude (I \propto A^2$), the intensity ratio between waxing and waning is:
\dfrac{I_\max}{I_\min} = \left(\dfrac{A_\max}{A_\min}\right)^2 = \left(\dfrac{9}{1}\right)^2 = \dfrac{81}{1}$

Thus, the observer will hear $4$ beats/s with an intensity ratio of $81 : 1$.

Answer: $4$ beats/s with intensity ratio $81 : 1$ between waxing and waning.

77075.subject: Mathematics
77075.text:
$What is the solution of the differential equation
\frac{d x}{d y}=\frac{x+y+1}{x+y-1} ?$
77075.sol:
Let $t=x+y \Rightarrow \frac{d t}{d y}=\frac{d x}{d y}+1$
So, $\frac{d t}{d y}-1=\frac{t+1}{t-1}\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d t}{d y}=\frac{t+1+t-1}{t-1}=\frac{2 t}{t-1} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \int \frac{t-1}{t} d t=2 \int d y \\
& \Rightarrow \quad t-\log t=2 y+\mathrm{C}_1 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad x+y-\log (x+y)-2 y=\mathrm{C}_1 \\
& \Rightarrow y-x+\log (x+y)=-\mathrm{C}_1=\mathrm{C}
\end{aligned}$

78057.subject: Mathematics
78057.text: The completion of a construction job may be delayed due to strike. The probability of strike is 0.6. The probability that the construction job gets completed on time if there is no strike is 0.85 and the probability that the construction job gets completed on time if there is a strike is 0.35. What is the probability that the construction job will not be completed on time?
78057.sol:
Let $E_1=$ strike; $E_2=$ no strike $F=$ Job completed on time.
$\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \quad P(F)=P\left(F / E_1\right) \cdot P\left(E_1\right)+P\left(F / E_2\right) \cdot P\left(E_2\right) \\
& =0.35 \times 0.6+0.4 \times 0.85=0.55 \\
& P(\bar{F})=P(\text{ Job not completed on time }) \\
& =1-0.55=0.45
\end{aligned}$

80100.subject: Botany
80100.sol:
The sweet potato root system consists of fibrous roots - that absorb nutrients and water and anchor the plant and storage roots - which are lateral roots that store photosynthetic products.

The root system of sweet potato plants obtained by vegetative propagation starts with adventitious roots that develop into primary fibrous roots which branch into lateral roots. As the plant matures, thick pencil roots that become lignified are produced. Other roots without lignin, are fleshy and bulky and are called storage roots. Such roots are specialized to store food and get swollen in the process.

Plants are grown from true seed form a typical root system with a central axle with lateral branches. Later on, the central axle functions as a storage root.

83542.subject: Physics
83542.text: Three identical p-n junction diodes $D_1$, $D_2$ and $D_3$ are connected across a battery as shown in the figure. If the width of the depletion regions of $D_1$, $D_2$ and $D_3$ are $W_1$, $W_2$ and $W_3$, respectively, then the correct option is :
83542.sol:
From the given circuit diagram, we can determine the biasing of each diode by observing their connections to the battery.

The battery symbol has its longer line on the left and shorter, thicker line on the right. This indicates that the left side of the circuit is connected to the positive terminal and the right side to the negative terminal.

1. For diode $D_1$: The p-side (triangle) is connected to the positive terminal (via a resistor) and the n-side (straight line) is connected to the negative terminal. Thus, $D_1$ is forward-biased.
2. For diode $D_2$: The p-side is connected to the positive terminal, but there is a clear break in the circuit on its n-side. Since it is an open circuit, no current flows through it, meaning $D_2$ is unbiased.
3. For diode $D_3$: The n-side is connected to the positive terminal and the p-side is connected to the negative terminal (via a resistor). Thus, $D_3$ is reverse-biased.

The width of the depletion region of a p-n junction depends on its biasing:
- In forward bias, the applied voltage opposes the built-in potential, causing the depletion width to decrease.
- In an unbiased state, the depletion width remains at its natural equilibrium value.
- In reverse bias, the applied voltage adds to the built-in potential, causing the depletion width to increase.

Let $W_{eq}$ be the equilibrium depletion width. Based on the biasing, we have:
$W_1 < W_{eq}$ (forward-biased)
$W_2 = W_{eq}$ (unbiased)
$W_3 > W_{eq}$ (reverse-biased)

Comparing these widths, we get the relation:
$W_3 > W_2 > W_1$

Answer: $W_3>W_2>W_1$

83684.subject: Physics
83684.text: Two Carnot engines $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ are operated in series. The engine $A$ receives heat from the source at temperature $T_1$ and rejects the heat to the sink at temperature $T$. The second engine $\mathrm{B}$ receives the heat at temperature $\mathrm{T}$ and rejects to its sink at temperature $T_2$. For what value of $T$ the efficiencies of the two engines are equal:
83684.sol:
We know that efficiency of carnot engine $\eta=1-\frac{T_2}{T_1}$
Where $T_1=$ temperature of source $T_2=$ temp of $\operatorname{sink}$ For engine $A, n_{\mathrm{A}}=1-\frac{T}{T_1}$ an engine $B, n_{\mathrm{B}}=1-\frac{T_2}{T}$ From question
$\begin{array}{l}
n_A =n_B \\
1-\frac{T}{T_1} =1-\frac{T_2}{T} \\
\Rightarrow \frac{T}{T_1}=\frac{T_2}{T} =\mathrm{T}^2 \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{T}^2 =\mathrm{T}_1 \mathrm{~T}_2 \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{T} =\sqrt{T_1 T_2}
\end{array}$

84186.subject: Zoology
84186.text: Which one of the following is a possibility for most of us in regard to breathing, by making a conscious effort?
options: One can breathe out air totally without oxygen
One can breathe out air through eustachian tubes by closing both the nose and the mouth
One can consiously breathe in and breathe out by moving the diaphragm alone, without moving the ribs at all
The lungs can be made fully empty by forcefully breathing out all air from them
84186.sol: The process of breathing involves the pathway of the human respiratory system and includes the nasal cavities, oral cavities, pharynx, trachea, primary bronchi, secondary bronchi and lungs with bronchioles and alveoli present. Breathing is a 2-fold process which includes breathing in and breathing out. During this process, the diaphragm which is the dome-shaped sheet of muscle located below the lungs contracts and expands along with the intercostal muscles to force air in and out of the lungs. Since intercostal muscles are also involved in the process of respiration, deeper respiration results in the movement of ribs too. Hence most of us can consciously breathe in and breathe out by moving the diaphragm alone.

85158.subject: Zoology
85158.text:
Match List I with List II :
List IList II
A. Incomplete dominanceI. Human skin colour
B. Co-dominanceII. Inheritance of flower colour in Antirrhinum sp.
C. PleiotropyIII. Phenylketonuria disease in humans
D. Polygenic inheritanceIV. ABO blood groups

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
85158.sol:
Incomplete dominance is observed in the inheritance of flower colour in Antirrhinum sp. (snapdragon), where the heterozygous phenotype is intermediate between the two homozygous phenotypes.

Co-dominance is exhibited by ABO blood groups in humans, where both alleles $I^A$ and $I^B$ express themselves fully in a heterozygous individual.

Pleiotropy occurs when a single gene influences multiple phenotypic traits. Phenylketonuria is an example of pleiotropy in humans, where a single gene mutation leads to mental retardation and a reduction in hair and skin pigmentation.

Polygenic inheritance involves traits controlled by three or more genes, such as human skin colour.

Therefore, the correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I.

Answer: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

The decreasing order of nucleophilicity for the following anions is
${\text{CH}_{3} {\text{CO}_{2}^{−} \text{,}{\text{CH}_{3} O^{−} \text{,}{C}_{6} {H}_{5} O^{−} \text{,}{\text{NO}_{3}^{−}$
88363.sol:
Since the electron donating atom is same, the nucleophilicity parallels basicity.
A conjugate base of a strong acid is weak and vice-versa.
The order of acidity is
$C{H}_{3}OH < {C}_{6}{H}_{5}OH < C{H}_{3}COOH < HN{O}_{3}$
Thus, the order of basicity and nucleophilicity is
$C{H}_{3}O^{-} > {C}_{6}{H}_{5}O^{-} > C{H}_{3}C{O}_{2}^{-} > N{O}_{3}^{-}$

Applying cosine formula in $\DeltaOAB$, we get

$cos{60}^{o} = \dfrac{O{A}^{2} + A{B}^{2} - O{B}^{2}}{2OA . AB}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{900 + {x}^{2} - 4900}{2 \times 30 \times x}$

$⇒ {x}^{2} - 30x - 4000 = 0$

$⇒ x = 80$

$AB = 80$ kms

Speed of ship =$10$ km/hr

$∴$ Time =$8$ hrs

Required number of students taking exactly one subject is

$= 120 + 90 + 60 - 2 \left(50\right) - 2 \left(50\right) - 2\left(43\right)$+ $3 \left(38\right)$
$= 98$

92701.text: A thin bar of length $L$ has a mass per unit length $\lambda$, that increases linearly with distance from one end. If its total mass is $M$ and its mass per unit length at the lighter end is ${λ}_{0}$,& then the distance of the centre of mass from the lighter end is
92701.sol:
$\lambda ∝ \text{x}$

$\lambda = \text{Kx} + {λ}_{0}$

$\text{dm} = \lambda \text{dx}$

$∴ {X}_{cm} = \dfrac{\mathop{∫}_{0}^{L} \text{dm} \cdot \text{x}}{\mathop{∫}_{0}^{L} \text{dm}} = \dfrac{\mathop{∫}_{0}^{L} \left(\text{Kx} + {λ}_{0}\right)\text{dx.x} }{\mathop{∫}_{0}^{L} \left(\text{Kx} + {λ}_{0}\right) \text{dx}}$

$= \dfrac{\text{K} \cdot {\left[\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right]}_{0}^{L} + {λ}_{0} {\left[\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\right]}_{0}^{L}}{\text{K} {\left[\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\right]}_{0}^{L} + {λ}_{0} \text{L}}$

$= \dfrac{\dfrac{{KL}^{3}}{3} + \dfrac{{λ}_{0} L^{2}}{2}}{\dfrac{{KL}^{2}}{2} + {λ}_{0} \text{L}}$

$= \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{\text{KL}}{3} + \dfrac{{λ}_{0}}{2}\right) L^{2}}{\dfrac{{KL}^{2}}{2} + {λ}_{0} \text{L}}$

Now, $\text{M} = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{L} \text{dm}$

$= \dfrac{{KL}^{2}}{2} + {λ}_{0} \text{L}$

$2 \text{M} = {KL}^{2} + 2 {λ}_{0} \text{L}$

$\text{K} = \dfrac{2 \left(\text{M} - {λ}_{0} \text{L}\right)}{L^{2}}$

Putting the value of K.

${X}_{cm} = \dfrac{\left\{\dfrac{2 \left(\text{M} - {λ}_{0} \text{L}\right)}{3 \text{L}} + \dfrac{{λ}_{0}}{2}\right\} L^{2}}{\text{M}}$

$= \dfrac{2 L^{2} \left(\text{M} - {λ}_{0} \text{L}\right)}{3 \text{LM}} + \dfrac{{λ}_{0} L^{2}}{2 \text{M}}$

$= \dfrac{2 \text{ML}}{3 \text{M}} - \dfrac{2 {λ}_{0} L^{2}}{3 \text{M}} + \dfrac{{λ}_{0} L^{2}}{2 \text{M}}$

$= \dfrac{2 \text{L}}{3} - \dfrac{{λ}_{0} L^{2}}{6 \text{M}}$

Hence, $\dfrac{2 \text{L}}{3} - \dfrac{{λ}_{0} L^{2}}{6 \text{M}}$

94691.text: Carbon monoxide is carried around a closed cyclic process $abc$, in which $bc$ is an isothermal process, as shown in the diagram. The gas absorbs $7000J$ of heat as its temperature is increased from $300K$ to $1000K$ in going from $a$ to $b$. The quantity of heat ejected by the gas during the process $ca$& is
94691.sol:
${\left(\Delta \text{Q}\right)}_{\text{ab}} = + 7 0 0 0 = \mu {\text{C}}_{\text{v}} \left(1 0 0 0 - 3 0 0\right)$               ...(i)

For the process $ca$:

${\text{T}}_{\text{a}} = 3 0 0 K$,  ${\text{T}}_{\text{c}} = {\text{T}}_{\text{b}} = 1 0 0 0 K$

${\left(\Delta \text{Q}\right)}_{\text{ca}} = \mu {\text{C}}_{\text{p}} \left(3 0 0 - 1 0 0 0\right) = - \mu {\text{C}}_{\text{p}} \times 7 0 0$

             $= - \mu \left({\text{C}}_{\text{v}} + \text{R}\right) 7 0 0$               ...(ii)

For carbon monoxide:

         ${\text{T}}_{\text{a}} = 3 0 0 K$,  ${\text{T}}_{\text{c}} = {\text{T}}_{\text{h}} = 1 0 0 0 K$

${\left(\Delta \text{Q}\right)}_{\text{ca}} = \mu {\text{C}}_{\text{p}} \left(3 0 0 - 1 0 0 0\right) = - \mu {\text{C}}_{\text{p}} \times 7 0 0$

             $= - \mu \left({\text{C}}_{\text{v}} + \text{R}\right) 7 0 0$

For carbon monoxide:

             $\gamma = \dfrac{7}{5}$

${\text{C}}_{\text{v}} = \dfrac{\text{R}}{\gamma - 1} = \dfrac{\text{R}}{\dfrac{7}{5} - 1} = \dfrac{5 \text{R}}{2}$               ...(iii)

Hence, from Eq. (i)

$7 0 0 0 = \mu \dfrac{5 \text{R}}{2} \times 7 0 0$ or  $\mu \text{R} = \dfrac{2 0}{5} = 4$

${\left(\Delta \text{Q}\right)}_{\text{ca}} = - \left(7 0 0 0 + 4 \times 7 0 0\right) = - 9 8 0 0 J$

Negative sign shows that heat is ejected.

In Planaria (flatworms), we observe true regeneration, i.e., a fragmented organism regenerates the lost part of its body and becomes a new organism. 100998.subject: Physics
100998.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
100998.text:
Assertion (A): In an elastic collision of two bodies, the momentum and energy of each body is conserved.
Reason (R): If two bodies stick to each other, after colliding, the collision is said to be perfectly inelastic.
options: Assertion (A) is True, Reason (R) is True; Reason (R) is a correct explanation for Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is True, Reason (R) is True; Reason (R) is not a correct explanation for Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is True, Reason (R) is False.
Assertion (A) is False, Reason (R) is True.
100998.sol:
- Assertion (A) is False.
- In an elastic collision, the total momentum of the system and the total kinetic energy of the system are conserved. Momentum and kinetic energy are not, in general, conserved for each body individually; they can exchange between bodies. So the phrase "of each body" makes A false.
- Reason (R) is True.
- When two bodies stick together after collision, the collision is perfectly inelastic by definition.
Therefore, the correct option is (4): Assertion (A) is False, Reason (R) is True.

Now, heat converted to work
$\begin{aligned}& =Q_1-Q_2 \\& =6.0 \times 10^4-4.8 \times 10^4 \\
& =1.2 \times 10^4 \mathrm{cal}\end{aligned}$

105618.text:
Assertion : A photon has no rest mass, yet it carries definite momentum.
Reason : Momentum of photon is due to its energy and hence its equivalent mass.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
105618.sol:
Equivalent mass of photon $(\mathrm{m})$ is given from equation
$E=m c^2=h v \quad \therefore m=\frac{h v}{c^2}$
where $E$ is energy, $m$ is mass, $c$ is speed of light, $h$ is Planck's constant, $v$ is frequency.
$\therefore \quad$ Momentum of photon $=\frac{h v}{c^2} \times c=\frac{h v}{c}$

116346.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Nitrogen exhibits a greater tendency for catenation compared to phosphorus.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
116346.sol:
Assertion (A) is false because the tendency of catenation in nitrogen is much less than that in phosphorus.

Reason (R) is true. Nitrogen has a small atomic size, which makes the N-N bond length very short. This leads to high interelectronic repulsion between the non-bonding electrons (lone pairs) on the adjacent nitrogen atoms.

As a result, the N-N single bond is weaker than the P-P single bond. This weak single bond is the very reason why nitrogen has a weaker catenation tendency.

Therefore, Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

117108.subject: Chemistry
117108.text:
In the group 4 transition metals, it is observed that the ratio of atomic radii $\dfrac{r(\text{Zr})}{r(\text{Ti})}$ is significantly greater than 1, whereas the ratio $\dfrac{r(\text{Hf})}{r(\text{Zr})}$ is approximately 1.

What is the primary reason for the ratio $\dfrac{r(\text{Hf})}{r(\text{Zr})}$ being approximately 1?
options: The poor shielding effect of the completely filled $4f$ orbitals in Hafnium
The enhanced shielding provided by the completely filled $5d$ orbitals in Hafnium
The poor shielding effect of $5f$ electrons in Hafnium
The inert pair effect operating on the $6s$ orbital electrons
117108.sol:
The atomic radius of Hafnium (Hf) is almost identical to that of Zirconium (Zr) due to the lanthanoid contraction. Before the $5d$ series begins, the $4f$ orbitals are completely filled with 14 electrons. The $4f$ electrons shield the increasing nuclear charge very poorly. This poor shielding causes a significant contraction in the size of the valence shell, which essentially cancels out the expected increase in size down the group from the $4d$ to the $5d$ series.

Hafnium does not contain $5f$ electrons, and the inert pair effect primarily applies to heavier p-block elements.

Answer: The poor shielding effect of the completely filled $4f$ orbitals in Hafnium

123107.subject: Botany
123107.text: In a longitudinal section of a root. Starting from the tip upward the four zones occur in the following order:
options: rootcap, cell division, cellenlargement, cell maturation
root cap, cell division, cell maturation, cell enlargement
cell division, cell enlargement, cell maturation, root cap
cell division, cell maturation, cell enlargement, root cap.
123107.sol:
The root tip can be divided into three zones: a zone of cell division, a zone of elongation, and a zone of maturation. The zone of cell division is closest to the root tip and is made up of the actively-dividing cells of the root meristem, which contains the undifferentiated cells of the germinating plant. The zone of elongation is where the newlyformed cells increase in length, thereby lengthening the root. zone of cell maturation where the root cells differentiate into specialized cell types.
Related Theory Root growth begins with seed germination. When the plant embryo emerges from the seed, the radicle of the embryo forms the root system. The tip of the root is protected by the root cap, a structure exclusive to roots and unlike any other plant structure. The root cap is continuously replaced because it is easily damaged as the root pushes through soil.

124362.subject: Botany
124362.text:
Read the following statements carefully:

(A) Robert Brown discovered the nucleus in 1831.
(B) Camillo Golgi first observed densely stained reticular structures near the nucleus.
(C) George Palade first observed ribosomes as dense particles under the light microscope.
(D) The material of the nucleus stained by acidic dyes was given the name chromatin by Flemming.

How many of the above statements are correct?
124362.sol:
Statement (A) is correct: Nucleus as a cell organelle was first described by Robert Brown as early as 1831.

Statement (B) is correct: Camillo Golgi (1898) first observed densely stained reticular structures near the nucleus, which were later named Golgi bodies after him.

Statement (C) is incorrect: George Palade (1953) first observed ribosomes as dense particles under the electron microscope, not the light microscope.

Statement (D) is incorrect: The material of the nucleus stained by basic dyes (not acidic dyes) was given the name chromatin by Flemming.

Therefore, exactly two statements (A and B) are correct.

Answer: Two

125177.subject: Botany
125177.text: Consider the complete aerobic oxidation of one molecule of glucose. How many molecules of $\text{NADH} + \text{H}^{+}$ and $\text{CO}_{2}$ are produced exclusively during the step catalyzed by the $\text{Mg}^{2+}$-dependent pyruvate dehydrogenase enzyme?
125177.sol:
The enzyme pyruvate dehydrogenase catalyzes the link reaction (oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate to acetyl CoA) in the mitochondrial matrix, which requires $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ions.

During glycolysis, one molecule of glucose is broken down into two molecules of pyruvate. Therefore, the link reaction occurs twice for every glucose molecule entering aerobic respiration.

Each single reaction of pyruvate forming acetyl CoA produces $1 \text{ NADH} + \text{H}^{+}$ and $1 \text{ CO}_{2}$.

For two molecules of pyruvate (derived from one glucose molecule), the total yield from this specific step is $2 \text{ NADH} + \text{H}^{+}$ and $2 \text{ CO}_{2}$.

Students who select $1 \text{ NADH} + \text{H}^{+}$ and $1 \text{ CO}_{2}$ fail to account for the two pyruvate molecules generated per glucose. Those selecting $6 \text{ NADH} + \text{H}^{+}$ and $4 \text{ CO}_{2}$ are incorrectly identifying the products of the Krebs cycle.

Answer: $2 \text{ NADH} + \text{H}^{+}$ and $2 \text{ CO}_{2}$

127588.subject: Botany
127588.text: How does the solar energy captured by plants flow through different organisms in an ecosystem?
127588.sol: :. Except for the deep sea hydro-thermal ecosystem, sun is the only source of energy for all ecosystems on Earth. Of the incident solar radiation less than 50 per cent of it is photosynthetically active radiation (PAR). We know that plants and photosynthetic bacteria (autotrophs), fix Sun’s radiant energy to make food from simple inorganic materials. Plants capture only 2-10 per cent of the PAR and this small amount of energy sustains the entire living world. So, it is very important to know how the solar energy captured by plants flows through different organisms of an ecosystem. All organisms are dependent for their food on producers, either directly or indirectly. So you find unidirectional flow of energy from the sun to producers and then to consumers. Is this in keeping with the first law of thermodynamics?

127605.subject: Botany
127605.text: What do decomposers absorb after breaking down dead and waste materials?
127605.sol:
.

The detritus food chain (DFC) begins with dead organic matter. It is made up of decomposers which are heterotrophic organisms, mainly fungi and bacteria. They meet their energy and nutrient requirements by degrading dead organic matter or detritus. These are also known as saprotrophs (sapro: to decompose). Decomposers secrete digestive enzymes that breakdown dead and waste materials into simple, inorganic materials, which are subsequently absorbed by them

127914.subject: Zoology
127914.text: How many digits do the fore limbs of frogs end in?
127914.sol: Have you ever touched the skin of frog? The skin is smooth and slippery due to the presence of mucus. The skin is always maintained in a moist condition. The colour of dorsal side of body is generally olive green with dark irregular spots. On the ventral side the skin is uniformly pale yellow. The frog never drinks water but absorb it through the skin. Body of a frog is divisible into head and trunk A neck and tail are absent. Above the mouth, a pair of nostrils is present. Eyes are bulged and covered by a nictitating membrane that protects them while in water. On either side of eyes a membranous tympanum (ear) receives sound signals. The forelimbs and hind limbs help in swimming, walking, leaping and burrowing. The hind limbs end in five digits and they are larger and muscular than fore limbs that end in four digits. Feet have webbed digits that help in swimming. Frogs exhibit sexual dimorphism. Male frogs can be distinguished by the presence of sound producing vocal sacs and also a copulatory pad on the first digit of the fore limbs which are absent in female frogs.

127988.subject: Zoology
127988.text: What is the double fold of peritoneum called that attaches the testes to the kidneys?
127988.sol: Frogs have well organised male and female reproductive systems. Male reproductive organs consist of a pair of yellowish ovoid testes , which are found adhered to the upper part of kidneys by a double fold of peritoneum called mesorchium. Vasa efferentia are 10-12 in number that arise from testes. They enter the kidneys on their side and open into Bidder’s canal. Finally it communicates with the urinogenital duct that comes out of the kidneys and opens into the cloaca. The cloaca is a small, median chamber that is used to pass faecal matter, urine and sperms to the exterior. The female reproductive organs include a pair of ovaries The ovaries are situated near kidneys and there is no functional connection with kidneys. A pair of oviduct arising from the ovaries opens into the cloaca separately. A mature female can lay 2500 to 3000 ova at a time. Fertilisation is external and takes place in water. Development involves a larval stage called tadpole. Tadpole undergoes metamorphosis to form the adult.Frogs are beneficial for mankind because they eat insects and protect the crop. Frogs maintain ecological balance because these serve as an important link of food chain and food web in the ecosystem. In some countries the muscular legs of frog are used as food by man.

128330.subject: Zoology
128330.text: What is the function of the thymus gland?
128330.sol: The thymus gland is a lobular structure located between lungs behind sternum on the ventral side of aorta. The thymus plays a major role in the development of the immune system. This gland secretes the peptide hormones called thymosins. Thymosins play a major role in the differentiation of T-lymphocytes, which provide cell-mediated immunity. In addition, thymosins also promote production of antibodies to provide humoral immunity. Thymus is degenerated in old individuals resulting in a decreased production of thymosins. As a result, the immune responses of old persons become weak.

128792.subject: Zoology
128792.text: What is the function of neutrophils in the body?
options: Destroy foreign organisms entering the body
Resisting infections and associated with allergic reactions
128792.sol: Leucocytes are also known as white blood cells (WBC) as they are colorless due to the lack of haemoglobin. They are nucleated and are relatively lesser in number which averages 6000-8000 mm–3 of blood. Leucocytes are generally short lived. We have two main categories of WBCs – granulocytes and agranulocytes. Neutrophils, eosinophils and basophils are different types of granulocytes, while lymphocytes and monocytes are the agranulocytes. Neutrophils are the most abundant cells (60-65 per cent) of the total WBCs and basophils are the least (0.5-1 per cent) among them. Neutrophils and monocytes (6-8 per cent) are phagocytic cells which destroy foreign organisms entering the body. Basophils secrete histamine, serotonin, heparin, etc., and are involved in inflammatory reactions. Eosinophils (2-3 per cent) resist infections and are also associated with allergic reactions. Lymphocytes (20-25 per cent) are of two major types – ‘B’ and ‘T’ forms. Both B and T lymphocytes are responsible for immune responses of the body.

130464.subject: Zoology
130464.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The joint between adjacent vertebrae in the vertebral column allows limited movement.

Reason (R): Synovial joints are characterised by the presence of a fluid-filled synovial cavity between the articulating surfaces of the two bones.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
130464.sol:
The Assertion (A) is true because adjacent vertebrae in the vertebral column are connected by cartilaginous joints, which permit limited movements.

The Reason (R) is also a true statement, as synovial joints are indeed characterised by a fluid-filled synovial cavity that allows considerable movement.

However, the Reason (R) does not explain the Assertion (A) because the limited movement of the vertebral column is due to the presence of cartilaginous joints, not synovial joints. Therefore, both statements are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

130867.subject: Zoology
130867.text: What is the structure of a mammary gland?
130867.sol: A functional mammary gland is characteristic of all female mammals. The mammary glands are paired structures (breasts) that contain glandular tissue and variable amount of fat. The glandular tissue of each breast is divided into 15-20 mammary lobes containing clusters of cells called alveoli (Figure 2.4). The cells of alveoli secrete milk, which is stored in the cavities (lumens) of alveoli. The alveoli open into mammary tubules. The tubules of each lobe join to form a mammary duct. Several mammary ducts join to form a wider mammary ampulla which is connected to lactiferous duct through which milk is sucked out

130938.subject: Zoology
130938.text: When are the first movements of the foetus usually observed in human pregnancy?
130938.sol:
The human pregnancy lasts 9 months. In human beings, after one month of pregnancy, the embryo’s heart is formed. The first sign of growing foetus may be noticed by listening to the heart sound carefully through the stethoscope. By the end of the second month of pregnancy, the foetus develops limbs and digits. By the end of 12 weeks (first trimester), most of the major organ systems are formed, for example, the limbs and external genital organs are well developed. The first movements of the foetus and appearance of hair on the head are usually observed during the fifth month. By the end of about 24 weeks (end of second trimester), the body is covered with fine hair, eye-lids separate, and eyelashes are formed. By the end of nine months of pregnancy, the foetus is fully developed and is ready for delivery.

.

131521.subject: Zoology
131521.text: What is the role of regulatory sequences in inheritance of a character?
options: They provide binding site for RNA polymerase
They define the end of transcription
They affect inheritance of a character
131521.sol: The coding sequences or expressed sequences are defined as exons. Exons are said to be those sequences that appear in mature or processed RNA. The exons are interrupted by introns. Introns or intervening sequences do not appear in mature or processed RNA. The split-gene arrangement further complicates the definition of a gene in terms of a DNA segment. Inheritance of a character is also affected by promoter and regulatory sequences of a structural gene. Hence, sometimes the regulatory sequences are loosely defined as regulatory genes, even though these sequences do not code for any RNA or protein.

131534.subject: Zoology
131534.text: How many codons would a permutation combination of 4x4x4 generate?
131534.sol: If determining the biochemical nature of genetic material and the structure of DNA was very exciting, the proposition and deciphering of genetic code were most challenging. In a very true sense, it required involvement of scientists from several disciplines – physicists, organic chemists, biochemists and geneticists. It was George Gamow, a physicist, who argued that since there are only 4 bases and if they have to code for 20 amino acids, the code should constitute a combination of bases. He suggested that in order to code for all the 20 amino acids, the code should be made up of three nucleotides. This was a very bold proposition, because a permutation combination of 43 (4 × 4 × 4) would generate 64 codons; generating many more codons than required.

131839.subject: Zoology
131839.text: A segment of eukaryotic chromatin contains exactly $2000$ base pairs of DNA. Assuming typical packaging, what is the total number of individual histone protein molecules present in the core octamers of this segment?
131839.sol:
According to NCERT, a typical nucleosome contains $200$ base pairs (bp) of DNA helix.

First, calculate the number of nucleosomes in the given segment:
Number of nucleosomes = $\dfrac{2000 \text{ bp}}{200 \text{ bp per nucleosome}} = 10$ nucleosomes.

Next, recall that the core of each nucleosome is formed by a histone octamer, which consists of $8$ histone protein molecules.

Total number of histone molecules in the core octamers = $10 \text{ nucleosomes} \times 8 \text{ histones per core} = 80$ histone molecules.

The value $10$ represents only the number of nucleosomes. The value $90$ incorrectly includes the H1 histone (which is outside the core octamer) for each nucleosome. The value $160$ would result from incorrectly assuming $100$ bp per nucleosome.

Answer: $80$

132052.subject: Zoology
132052.text: How many true-breeding pea plant varieties did Mendel select?
132052.sol: Mendel conducted such artificial pollination/cross pollination experiments using several true-breeding pea lines. A true breeding line is one that, having undergone continuous self-pollination, shows the stable trait inheritance and expression for several generations. Mendel selected 14 true-breeding pea plant varieties, as pairs which were similar except for one character with contrasting traits. Some of the contrasting traits selected were smooth or wrinkled seeds, yellow or green seeds, inflated (full) or constricted green or yellow pods and tall or dwarf plants

133004.subject: Zoology
133004.text: Industrial melanism is an example of:
133004.sol: One of the most striking examples, which demonstrates the action of natural selection, is the industrial melanism in England. The peppered moth Biston betularia, with a dull grey colour, was abundant in England before the industrial revolution. A black coloured form of the same moth (melanic, a dominant mutant differing in a single gene), Biston carbonaria, was very rare. After industrial revolution, the proportion of Biston carbonaria, increased to almost 90 percent.
